exercises.prompt: Dobar dan! Ja sam Marko. Ja sam kovač.
exercises.translation: Good day! I am Marko. I am a blacksmith.
exercises.instruction: Greet him and say you are a traveller.
exercises.grammarTip: After “biti” (to be) the noun stays in the nominative, its dictionary form: Ja sam kovač. Ja sam putnik.

exercises.instruction: Tell him you need a sword.
exercises.grammarTip: The thing you need is the direct object, so it takes the accusative. For masculine nouns that name objects, the accusative looks the same as the nominative: mač → mač.

exercises.prompt: Imam mač i sjekiru. Što želite?
exercises.translation: I have a sword and an axe. What do you want?
exercises.grammarTip: Feminine nouns that end in -a change -a to -u in the accusative: sjekira → sjekiru. Marko used the same form: Imam … sjekiru.

exercises.prompt: Vidite li mog pomoćnika? On ima vašu sjekiru.
exercises.translation: Do you see my assistant? He has your axe.
exercises.grammarTip: Masculine nouns that name people or animals add -a in the accusative: pomoćnik → pomoćnika. Objects do not change: mač → mač.

exercises.prompt: Izvolite! Ovo je vaša nova sjekira.
exercises.translation: Here you go! This is your new axe.
exercises.instruction: Thank him and say you have a new axe.
exercises.grammarTip: An adjective takes the same case as its noun. After “Ovo je” both are nominative: nova sjekira. After “imam” both are accusative: novu sjekiru.
